status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 DOJ had not announced an enforcement campaign under 18 U.S.C. 1461 or 1462 against mailed abortion pills, issued a new Comstock Act opinion, or brought a case. The Office of Legal Counsel's opinions page lists ten opinions dated 2026-07-16 through 2026-09-17, none concerning the Comstock Act, and the page for the December 2022 opinion (which read the statute as not barring mailing of such drugs where the sender lacks intent of unlawful use) shows no withdrawal. At his 2026-07-15 confirmation hearing, Attorney General nominee Todd Blanche agreed to review that opinion; anti-abortion groups wrote to him on 2026-08-07 urging the review, and he was confirmed on 2026-08-08 and sworn in on 2026-08-10. On 2026-09-09 a DOJ attorney argued before the Fifth Circuit in Louisiana v. FDA (No. 26-30203) that Louisiana lacks standing and opposed its requested stay of the FDA's mifepristone rules; the reporting on that argument does not mention the Comstock Act. Reports describe the administration as leaving the existing mifepristone mail-distribution rules in place pending an FDA safety review whose timeline OSV News describes as unclear.

timeline.event: Context before the tracking window: the Office of Legal Counsel issues an opinion concluding that 18 U.S.C. 1461 does not prohibit mailing certain drugs that can be used for abortions when the sender lacks intent that the recipient use them unlawfully; DOJ's page for the opinion (updated 2023-01-03) shows no withdrawal.
Lawfare's list of the 14 memos Attorney General Bondi signed on her first day (death penalty, DEI, sanctuary jurisdictions, cartels, and others) does not include a Comstock Act directive.

At his Senate Judiciary Committee confirmation hearing, Todd Blanche agrees, after questions from Sens. Cruz and Cornyn, to carefully review DOJ's existing opinion on the Comstock Act. No policy change is announced.

Advancing American Freedom and a coalition of anti-abortion groups (reports give counts from about 30 to more than 80 signers; the Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission's president signed) send Blanche a letter asking him to review and reverse the 2022 opinion and to use DOJ's authority under the Comstock Act over mailed abortion drugs.

Blanche is sworn in as Attorney General after Senate confirmation in the early hours of 2026-08-08, according to OSV News. As of 2026-08-11 reports, no outcome of the review, new opinion, or enforcement action had been announced.

At Fifth Circuit argument in State of Louisiana v. FDA (No. 26-30203), a DOJ attorney argues Louisiana lacks standing and opposes its request for a stay of the FDA's 2023 mifepristone dispensing changes, and declines to discuss the FDA's ongoing review; the Bloomberg Law report does not mention the Comstock Act.
